issues.description: Method getStockIngredients has conflicting return types across artifacts. In the template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) the method is declared as 'public List<StockIngredient> getStockIngredients()' returning a List<StockIngredient>, while in the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) it is declared as 'public StockIngredient[] getStockIngredients()' returning a StockIngredient[] array. The problem statement's UML also models Stock as holding multiple StockIngredient instances via the 'stockIngredients' relation (implying an array/collection of StockIngredient). This mismatch is confusing because the exercise and provided helper utilities (ArrayHelpers) and the solution expect array semantics for stockIngredients, whereas the template's List return type encourages a different API. Students may be blocked or uncertain whether to use arrays or collections when implementing SealSaloon and when interacting with ArrayHelpers and other example code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of Stock.getStockIngredients consistent. Preferred fix: change the template implementation to 'public StockIngredient[] getStockIngredients()' (returning the internal array) so it matches the solution and the expected use of ArrayHelpers and the exercise examples. Alternatively, update the solution and problem text to consistently use List<StockIngredient> throughout (and adapt ArrayHelpers usage). Ensure all examples and helper usages in Main and SealSaloon are updated to match the chosen type.
